refinement.detail: The measured experiments found a smaller useful next layer: generate a normalized semantic effect plan (response class, order/cardinality, semantic command fields, projection obligations) and generic correlated bundle/journal/snapshot utilities, while leaving concrete service values project-owned. summary: Validated three preregistered effect-provider projects; Python V0 is a conditional go with parser, semantic-plan, signature, replay, bypass, and Java sequencing recommendations.

assertions: The three named projects exercise explicit DI, legacy monkeypatching, and ordered multi-provider state respectively; none requires a framework code change to add its provider.
Expected behavior, cost hypotheses, semantic bug classes, and mutant matrix are committed before validation runs, so success is not defined post hoc.
Every project has a green control, content/value assertions, more than one deterministic seed, a recorded replay proof for at least one failure, and cleanup/isolation proof.
The report distinguishes bugs killed by TLA-derived case semantics from bugs killed only by provider-owned assertions and from survivors/bypasses.
Results include exact counts/timings/footprints and an honest cost-benefit verdict per project plus one overall go/no-go recommendation.
Surviving mutants, bypasses, nondeterminism, or documentation failures remain visible as findings and become prioritized follow-up recommendations rather than being deleted or tuned away.
The examples and effectProviderExamples graph run green from a fresh checkout of the epic branch.
Host workflow remains zero-model-delta unless new observable CLI behavior landed; each example's own TLA+ model is checked with TLC and its generated cases are the cases actually fuzzed.

implementation_scope: predeclared hypotheses/mutants, raw run evidence, comparison report, and recommendations
ticket.objective: Validate the architecture as a measurement, not a showcase, with three independently onboarded projects and predeclared predictions: (A) an explicitly injected atomic document publisher — predicted high mutation yield at low integration cost; (B) a legacy HTTP client with retries/timeouts and a self-installed patch provider — predicted useful protocol bugs but higher monkeypatch/bypass friction; (C) a stateful multi-provider outbox workflow (store/queue plus clock/notification) — predicted highest semantic value and highest composition/modeling cost. Each project owns its TLA+ model, generated cases, application, adapter, providers, predeclared mutants, and validation record. Run green controls and every mutant with multiple deterministic seeds, prove replay and cleanup, and add a Test Graph node that validates all three. Measure authoring footprint, retrieval surface, generated states/cases, runtime, provider/adapter code, mutation kills by semantic bug class, bypasses, unsupported effects, run-to-run divergence, and whether an agent can onboard using the shipped docs without framework changes. Record findings before fixing them. Produce a go/no-go recommendation and a prioritized backlog for effectful modeling, including whether a standard response-plan schema, stronger bypass detection, or Java belongs next.
ticket.title: Three effectful-modeling projects, mutation evidence, and recommendation
